sections.h2: Where the Putnam County Register of Deeds sits and what it keeps
sections.html:
Find the register in Room 3 of the courthouse at 300 E Spring St, Cookeville, TN 38501. The counter is staffed from 8:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, and the line to call is 931-526-7101.

Everything that touches title to Putnam County land ends up in this office: deeds, mortgages, releases, plats, powers of attorney, and liens of every sort, from judgment and materialman's liens to state and federal tax liens. The books begin in 1854, when the county was re-established after earlier courts had dissolved it. Copies of recorded paperwork are available to anyone who asks, whether they walk in, phone, write or send an email. Military discharge papers (DD-214) are the one category held back from the public.

Staff will talk you through a fee, but writing a deed is outside what they can do. On a typical sale a title company or attorney drafts the instrument, and the register files it after the tax is paid.

Deeds and trust deeds are priced per thousand dollars, with page, clerk and flat charges layered on. Anything filed electronically also carries a $2.00 fee, which began July 1, 2023.

Putnam County recording fees by document type
Document typeFee charged by the county
Warranty deed$3.70 per thousand, $5.00 per page (2 page minimum), $1.00 clerk fee, $2.00 EDP fee
Trust deed (mortgage)$1.15 per thousand after the first $2,000, plus the same page, clerk and EDP fees
ModificationCharged like a trust deed, with no $2,000 deduction
Release$10.00 plus $2.00 EDP fee, $5.00 for each extra reference
Other documents$5.00 per page (2 page minimum), $5.00 for each added page, plus $2.00 EDP fee
Fixture filing$13.00 plus $2.00 EDP fee, $15.00 for each added name
DD-214 dischargeFree

Because the page count changes the total, phone 931-526-7101 if your packet has unusual attachments and ask staff to tally it before you come in.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Putnam County sale
sections.html:
The state's realty transfer tax runs $0.37 on every $100. Revenue Department guidance treats the purchase price as the base, and its help desk adds that the greater of the price paid or the property's value is generally used, under Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409. The $3.70 per thousand on the county's warranty deed line expresses the same rate.

A borrower's lender triggers a second tax, the indebtedness tax of $0.115 per $100 after the first $2,000, collected when the trust deed is filed. The flat page, clerk and EDP fees ride along with both taxes.

A seller's biggest saving here is knowing the number early. Ask your title agent which side of the table the contract assigns each tax to, and confirm the figure used as the sale price matches the contract, since the oath and the tax follow from it.

Which party pays each line is a matter for the purchase contract and your title agent. Request a written estimate of both taxes and the recording charges ahead of closing, so the numbers on the settlement statement hold still.

sections.h2: What the register needs before it will accept a document
sections.html:
The register keeps a seven-point checklist. Miss one item and the clerk will hand the paperwork back.

  • An original or a certified copy.
  • The name of whoever prepared it.
  • Both grantor and grantee named.
  • The date it was signed.
  • An Oath of Consideration on any deed.
  • The maximum principal indebtedness on any deed of trust.
  • A notary statement together with the notary seal.

The oath deserves care because the transfer tax is figured from it. Write down the true price or value, and have your title agent look at that number before anyone signs.

sections.h2: Searching records and protecting yourself from deed fraud
sections.html:
Records can be searched in person at the courthouse, or from home through US Title Search, which bills a monthly subscription. The register's staff can also tell you the year a house was built by checking its tax card, and the Assessor's Office keeps the same detail.

One free tool worth knowing is My Land Alert, at mylandalert.com, which the register recommends. It emails you whenever a document is recorded under your name or your business name. Landlords and owners who live out of town benefit most, since an alert lets you catch a deed you never signed within days and not years.

sections.h2: How do you fix or change a recorded deed?
sections.html:
Nobody can edit a deed once it is on the books. Adding or removing a name takes a brand new deed, drafted by an attorney or title agency and then recorded with the right oath and fees.

Putnam County allows owners to write their own deed, yet the register advises against it and will not help prepare one. A do-it-yourself deed missing a required line is turned away, and that can stall a closing. After a mortgage is paid, the lender sends the release to the register, and you may ask for a copy once it is recorded.

sections.h2: Recording the deed when you sell
sections.html:
Whether the house is in Cookeville, Algood, Baxter, Monterey or open country, the deed goes to the same courthouse counter. A sale usually unfolds like this.

  1. Your title company or attorney drafts the deed with grantor, grantee, preparer, date, Oath of Consideration and notary block.
  2. Someone reviews the price or value on the oath so the transfer tax comes out right.
  3. The original or a certified copy is delivered, with the tax and recording fees.
  4. If a mortgage is being paid off, the lender's release arrives on its own track, and a new buyer loan brings a separate trust deed.
  5. Once it is filed, request a copy of what was recorded and keep it with your closing papers.

When a buyer pays cash and takes the house as-is, the deed may be the only paper that reaches the register, so the visit goes quickly if everything is in order.

Putnam County covers 403 square miles on Central Time, with Cookeville as the seat and largest city. The Census estimate is 86,612 residents on July 1, 2025, up 8.4 percent from the 2020 base. There are 38,375 housing units, and owners live in 61.2 percent of homes. Median rent is $908 and median household income is $58,912. Monthly owner costs have a median of $1,450 with a mortgage and $446 without one.

faqs.q: What does a warranty deed cost to record in Putnam County?
faqs.a: The county adds $3.70 per thousand dollars of value, $5.00 a page with a two-page minimum, a $1.00 clerk fee and a $2.00 EDP fee. Phone 931-526-7101 to have staff total it for your document.

faqs.q: Where is the Putnam County register and how do I reach it?
faqs.a: Room 3 of the courthouse, 300 E Spring St, Cookeville, TN 38501, at 931-526-7101. Walk-in hours run 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: Is an Oath of Consideration required on a Putnam County deed?
faqs.a: Yes, every deed carries one, and a deed of trust has to show the maximum principal indebtedness. The transfer tax is based on the oath, so the figure should be accurate.

faqs.q: Can anyone request a copy of a recorded Putnam County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. All recorded documents are public except DD-214 discharge papers. Ask in person, by phone, by mail or by email.

faqs.q: Can I put another name on my Putnam County deed myself?
faqs.a: Not by editing it. The change needs a new deed, and the register suggests an attorney or title agency write it, because the office cannot help draft one.
